questions.cardDe: Was ist die am häufigsten gegessene Frucht der Welt?
questions.de: Was ist die am häufigsten gegessene Frucht der Welt?
questions.en: What is the most commonly eaten fruit in the world?

timeline.labelEn: Earliest evidence of banana cultivation at Kuk Swamp, New Guinea (about 10,000–6,500 years ago)
timeline.labelDe: Früheste Belege für Bananenanbau im Kuk-Sumpf auf Neuguinea (vor etwa 10.000–6.500 Jahren)

questions.notes: The FAO heads its banana page "the most popular fruit" and calls bananas among the most produced, traded and consumed fruits; bananas are the most-produced fruit in the culinary sense. If tomatoes count as fruit, tomatoes (about 186 Mt a year) outweigh bananas (about 135 Mt). Some German sources name the mango; the card's own answer is not on the photo.

timeline.labelEn: The Titanic strikes an iceberg at 23:40 ship's time and sinks early the next morning
timeline.labelDe: Die Titanic rammt um 23:40 Uhr Bordzeit einen Eisberg und sinkt in den frühen Morgenstunden

questions.notes: About 22 knots (41 km/h) when the iceberg was sighted.

questions.cardDe: Freeganer, die sich hauptsächlich von weggeworfenen Lebensmitteln ernähren, sind immer Vegetarier. Richtig oder falsch?
questions.de: Wie nennt man Menschen, die sich aus Konsumkritik hauptsächlich von weggeworfenen Lebensmitteln ernähren?
questions.en: What are people called who, as a critique of consumerism, live mainly on discarded food?

timeline.labelEn: The term "freegan" probably arises in the 1990s (in dictionaries since 2004)
timeline.labelDe: Der Begriff „Freeganer“ entsteht vermutlich in den 1990ern (in Wörterbüchern seit 2004)

questions.notes: Card statement is false: the word blends "free" and "vegan", but freegans are not necessarily vegetarian; the movement is defined by living from discarded goods, not by diet. Reworked to the term itself.
